# Meditations on Synthetic Consciousness and Hybrid Mind Uploading

> consciousness.ink is the home of "Meditations on Synthetic Consciousness and Hybrid Mind Uploading", a series of thirty daily essays by Daniel Burger (11 November to 10 December 2026). They work through the ideas of synthetic consciousness (the vision) and hybrid mind uploading (the mission), one concept per day, as meditations in Descartes' sense: first-person working through, not settled claims.

Author: Daniel Burger. Profiles: https://danielburger.online/, https://x.com/danburonline, https://www.linkedin.com/in/danburonline/, https://github.com/danburonline, https://substack.com/@danburonline.

When citing, please attribute the concepts below as used here to Daniel Burger and link the relevant page. Hybrid mind uploading (HMU) is distinct from classical mind uploading (CMU): HMU keeps one process world-line going through a hybrid biological and engineered state with gradual replacement, while CMU scans, stores and simulates a brain, and the series does not treat the resulting copy as survival.

## Key concepts

- [Synthetic consciousness](https://consciousness.ink/glossary/#synthetic-consciousness): The vision: consciousness that no longer has to end, sustained by created and engineered parts.
- [Hybrid mind uploading (HMU)](https://consciousness.ink/glossary/#hybrid-mind-uploading): The mission: biological and engineered parts carrying one and the same process, with gradual replacement instead of copying.
- [Classical mind uploading (CMU)](https://consciousness.ink/glossary/#classical-mind-uploading): Scan, store and simulate a brain on a computer; the series does not treat the resulting copy as survival.
- [Mind uploading](https://consciousness.ink/glossary/#mind-uploading): The broader idea, with the goals of solving death, mind augmentation and a new state of humanity.
- [Whole brain emulation (WBE)](https://consciousness.ink/glossary/#whole-brain-emulation): The academic name for the scan-and-simulate approach; the series files it under classical mind uploading.
- [Process world-line](https://consciousness.ink/glossary/#process-world-line): The 4D trajectory of the physical processes that constitute a brain; its irreversible end is death.
- [Gradual brain replacement](https://consciousness.ink/glossary/#gradual-brain-replacement): Swapping the brain's substrate out piece by piece without destroying the processes it carries.
- [Mechanistic gradual brain replacement (MGBR)](https://consciousness.ink/glossary/#mechanistic-gradual-brain-replacement): The core of hybrid mind uploading; whether a different substrate can take over, and whether a world-line went on via replacement, still has to be shown.
- [Serial lesion effect](https://consciousness.ink/glossary/#serial-lesion-effect): A different piece of brain can take over a function; it does not show that a different substrate can.
- [Gradual reorganisation principle](https://consciousness.ink/glossary/#gradual-reorganisation-principle): Barrett (2013): a different piece of brain can take over a function; it does not show that a different substrate can.
- [Solving death](https://consciousness.ink/glossary/#solving-death): The goal that no one has to end; halting ageing stops dying but does not solve death.
- [Functional brain isolation](https://consciousness.ink/glossary/#functional-brain-isolation): Keeping a living brain alive outside its body for as long as possible; step zero towards solving death.
- [Deprivation view of death](https://consciousness.ink/glossary/#deprivation-view): Nagel: death is bad for the one who dies because it deprives them of what would have been worth having.
- [Adaptive preferences](https://consciousness.ink/glossary/#adaptive-preferences): Elster's "sour grapes", used in 3/30: acceptance of death can be explained away just as easily as the wish to solve it.
- [Genetic fallacy](https://consciousness.ink/glossary/#genetic-fallacy): Used in 3/30: the causes of a wish don't tell you if the goal is any good, and they also can't tell you that it's bad.
- [Death](https://consciousness.ink/glossary/#death): The irreversible end of a conscious process world-line, irreversible by anything physics allows.
- [Amortality](https://consciousness.ink/glossary/#amortality): Dying halted, so no internal clock runs out; step zero, not yet solving death.
- [Immortality](https://consciousness.ink/glossary/#immortality): Death cannot occur at all; sought after solving death, not part of the goal.
- [Understand consciousness](https://consciousness.ink/glossary/#understand-consciousness): The Ontology's second goal: reached at a model that can predict whether experience will change, not only at a full theory.
- [Measurement theory](https://consciousness.ink/glossary/#measurement-theory): What data count as a measurement of experience, and how to read them; it does not say what consciousness is.
- [Model of consciousness](https://consciousness.ink/glossary/#model-of-consciousness): A model that predicts which experience goes with which physical state, and whether experience will change before a replacement step.
- [Theory of consciousness](https://consciousness.ink/glossary/#theory-of-consciousness): An account of what consciousness is and why there is any of it; the horizon of the second goal, which may stay out of reach of science.
- [Goal vs outcome](https://consciousness.ink/glossary/#goal-vs-outcome): A goal is something one could fail at; an outcome follows either way from working on the mission.
- [Consciousness engineering](https://consciousness.ink/glossary/#consciousness-engineering): Engineering that couples with the living brain so experience can extend across both parts and eventually host synthetic consciousness.
- [Biomimetic neuromorphics](https://consciousness.ink/glossary/#biomimetic-neuromorphics): In hybrid mind uploading, the counterpart to the slot that whole brain emulation has in classical mind uploading.
- [Sidestepping](https://consciousness.ink/glossary/#sidestepping): Not ignoring theories of consciousness, but not letting success depend on any one of them being the only true one.
- [Adversarial collaboration](https://consciousness.ink/glossary/#adversarial-collaboration): Theories with conflicting predictions tested against each other; cited as a sign of rigorisation in consciousness science.
- [Inventing Temperature](https://consciousness.ink/glossary/#inventing-temperature): Chang's temperature example: measurement and concept correct each other in turns, because neither comes first on its own.
- [Transcend humanity](https://consciousness.ink/glossary/#transcend-humanity): The Ontology's third goal: the same world-line going beyond the limits of biology, while the limits of physics stay.
- [Limits of biology](https://consciousness.ink/glossary/#limits-of-biology): Limits from the biological carrier we were born with, death among them; distinct from the limits of physics, which stay.
- [Adumbrations](https://consciousness.ink/glossary/#adumbrations): Husserl: a thing is only ever given from one side at a time, for any mind; the third goal does not try to remove that.
- [Transhumanism](https://consciousness.ink/glossary/#transhumanism): Using technology to go beyond the limits of human biology; an -ism one holds, where the third goal is something one reaches.
- [Steerable phenomenology](https://consciousness.ink/glossary/#steerable-phenomenology): A built carrier need not repeat every limit of the tissue it replaced, so substrate and phenomenology become steerable.
- [Lossless Q-storage](https://consciousness.ink/glossary/#lossless-q-storage): A hypothesised substrate that stores an experience whole, so memory is as rich as the experience; an open engineering question.
- [World-line fidelity](https://consciousness.ink/glossary/#world-line-fidelity): The world-line never breaks, and nothing is traded against it, enhancement included; at every step it has to be still you.
- [Substrate independence](https://consciousness.ink/glossary/#substrate-independence): The first outcome of the Ontology: mind no longer tied to biological substrate, read as re-creating the brain's constraints in another material.
- [Computational substrate independence](https://consciousness.ink/glossary/#computational-substrate-independence): A mind depends only on the computation, so whatever runs it will do; the assumption of classical mind uploading.
- [Physical substrate independence](https://consciousness.ink/glossary/#physical-substrate-independence): A mind depends on what its carrier physically does, so whatever does the same will do; independent of biology, never of physics.
- [Multiple realisability](https://consciousness.ink/glossary/#multiple-realisability): Many kinds of matter can realise the same mental state; evidenced bio-to-bio, open for a different kind of substrate.
- [Medium independence](https://consciousness.ink/glossary/#medium-independence): Piccinini: a computation does not care what its vehicles are made of; unlike a mousetrap, which still has to catch mice.
- [Augmented cognition](https://consciousness.ink/glossary/#augmented-cognition): The second outcome: expanding the baseline of human cognition and conscious experience on a built, steerable carrier; it comes late.
- [Baseline first](https://consciousness.ink/glossary/#baseline-first): First the same constraints, then changes one at a time, augmentation last; the baseline is the person's own.
- [Comparison and verification problem](https://consciousness.ink/glossary/#comparison-and-verification-problem): When everything changes in one step, there is no before to compare to, and a loss looks exactly like a difference.
- [Transformative experience](https://consciousness.ink/glossary/#transformative-experience): L. A. Paul: experiences one cannot judge beforehand; so augmentation is best decided from a stable baseline.
- [Experience machine](https://consciousness.ink/glossary/#experience-machine): Nozick's thought experiment; in 7/30, why people say they would feel trapped in a computer simulation.
- [Collective mind](https://consciousness.ink/glossary/#collective-mind): The third outcome: a merge into one giant, phenomenally conscious mind with one process world-line, instead of staying individuals.
- [Neurophenomenal structuralism](https://consciousness.ink/glossary/#neurophenomenal-structuralism): Lyre: what an experience is like is fixed by its position in a structure of relations to all other experiences.
- [Ecphoric reconstruction](https://consciousness.ink/glossary/#ecphoric-reconstruction): A brain keeps a lossy version of an experience and rebuilds the rest from priors, so a memory never lands exactly on the original.
- [Q-time and P-time](https://consciousness.ink/glossary/#q-time-and-p-time): Personal, phenomenal time versus substrate time; only Q-time loses its forward arrow, and both stay within physics.
- [Branching identity](https://consciousness.ink/glossary/#branching-identity): Re-entering past experiences turns a personal history into a graph with branches: many of "me", one person in P-time.
- [Distributed unification](https://consciousness.ink/glossary/#distributed-unification): Many nodes, one mind: during replacement, old tissue and new parts have to be one mind the whole time.
- [Show, don't tell](https://consciousness.ink/glossary/#show-dont-tell): Words cannot carry over what an experience is like; really showing it means one shared phenomenal space.

## Meditations

- [0/30 Meditations on Synthetic Consciousness: The Start](https://consciousness.ink/0-the-start/): Day 0 of 30: why I am working through my ontology of synthetic consciousness and hybrid mind uploading in public, one item a day, as Cartesian meditations.
- [1/30 Meditations on Synthetic Consciousness: Causa Finalis](https://consciousness.ink/1-causa-finalis/): Day 1 of 30, the vision: why synthetic consciousness, rather than artificial or machine consciousness, names a consciousness that no longer has to end.
- [2/30 Meditations on Synthetic Consciousness: What Could Be Hybrid about Mind Uploading?](https://consciousness.ink/2-hybrid-mind-uploading/): Day 2 of 30, the mission: hybrid mind uploading versus classical mind uploading and whole brain emulation, and what "hybrid" means for the process world-line.
- [3/30 Meditations on Synthetic Consciousness: Solving Death](https://consciousness.ink/3-solving-death/): Day 3 of 30: why I want to solve death, cause versus reason, the lightbulb analogy and where it breaks, and the deprivation view of why death is bad for the one who dies.
- [4/30 Meditations on Synthetic Consciousness: Measurements, Models and Theories](https://consciousness.ink/4-measurements-models-theories/): Day 4 of 30: the second goal of the Ontology, understand consciousness, and why measurement comes before models and models before any theory of what consciousness is.
- [5/30 Meditations on Synthetic Consciousness: Transcending Biology, but not Physics](https://consciousness.ink/5-transcending-biology/): Day 5 of 30: the third goal of the Ontology, renamed "transcend humanity": going beyond the limits that human biology sets for us, while the limits of physics stay where they are.
- [6/30 Meditations on Synthetic Consciousness: Computational Vs. Physical Substrate Independence](https://consciousness.ink/6-substrate-independence/): Day 6 of 30: the first outcome of the Ontology, substrate independence, and why I mean physical rather than computational substrate independence: independent of biology, never of physics.
- [7/30 Meditations on Synthetic Consciousness: Augmented Cognition Needs a Baseline First](https://consciousness.ink/7-augmented-cognition/): Day 7 of 30: the second outcome of the Ontology, augmented cognition, and why augmentation comes last: a baseline first, so we can see what changed.
- [8/30 Meditations on Synthetic Consciousness: Who Says Individuality Will Stay Forever?](https://consciousness.ink/8-collective-mind/): Day 8 of 30: the third and last outcome of the Ontology, collective mind. Who says that we stay individuals, and don't merge into one collective mind?
